center_distance.description:
The least distance between the elements' centres (a vertex's point, a circle's or
arc's centre, a cylinder face's axis as an infinite line), if both have one.

center_to_element.description:
Where one element has a centre (a vertex's point, a circle's or arc's centre, a
cylinder face's axis) and the other is a planar face or a straight edge: a point
centre's least distance from the other as bounded, as FreeCAD's Quick Measure gives a
hole's centre to a face or an edge (so where the foot of its perpendicular falls off
the face, the distance to the nearest point of the face's boundary); a cylinder's
axis's distance from the infinite plane or line it's parallel to, ignoring its
bounds, at exactly 0 degrees, and null if it isn't (Silico's own, which FreeCAD's
Quick Measure doesn't give). Null otherwise.

distance.description:
The least distance between the elements as bounded (never their infinite carriers),
in mm: 0 where they touch or cross.

from.description:
A point where it's met, on the first element: with `to`, one pair of points where
it's met (the pair first by its points' coordinates), a witness, not an identity.

normal_distance.description:
Where both are straight edges or planar faces at exactly 0 or 180 degrees: two faces
or two edges, the perpendicular distance from the second's reference point (a face's
centre of area, an edge's midpoint) to the first's plane or line; an edge and a face,
the edge's midpoint's from the face's plane, whichever comes first. Null otherwise.

to.description: The pair's point on the second element.

session.description: The session as the command left it: null for a command that takes no session.

tools.description: A PNG of the model's bodies from a named view or a camera, with elements highlighted, returned as an image beside the result, and written to `to` in the workspace if given. After an edit, read with `model: "current"`, which waits for the edit's rebuild; `published` answers at once from the newest model rebuilt, which may be older.

Angle.description: An angle in degrees: a number, to at most 9 decimals (nanodegrees). An exponent is read exactly; Silico writes plain decimals. (Strings are reserved for expressions, which aren't read yet.)

Camera.description:
A camera: where it looks from and at, which way is up in the image, and how much it
sees. The document is Z-up. A result's camera can be passed back unchanged.

eye.description:
The eye, in global coordinates (mm), within 1e12 mm of the origin, at least a
nanometre from the target. An orthographic view uses only its direction from the
target; a perspective eye mustn't be inside a body or on its surface.

field_of_view.description:
A perspective camera's vertical angle, in degrees, from 0.001 to 179.999; null for
an orthographic camera.

target.description: What the view is centred on, in global coordinates (mm).

up.description:
Which way is up in the image: any vector with a part across the view, made
perpendicular to the view and of unit length in a result.

view_height.description:
An orthographic camera's view's height, in mm, from 1e-6 to 1e12; null for a
perspective camera.

NamedView.description:
A named view, as Fusion's ViewCube names them, the document Z-up: `front` looks from
−Y, `right` from +X, `top` from +Z, and the corners combine them.

Projection.description:
How a camera projects: from the eye in parallel (`orthographic`, as every named view
is), or from the eye as a point (`perspective`).

to.description:

cache; or null.

view.description: A named view, fitted to the bodies; null with a camera.
